title: Coexistence of superconductivity and magnetic order in BaFe$_2$S$_3$: evidence for orbital-selective delocalization
authors: Y. Oubaid, N. S. Dhami, P. Fertey, C. V. Colin, C. Ritter, A. Forget, D. Bounoua, J. -P. Rueff, M. Verseils, P. Foury-Leylekian, V. Balédent
abstract: Understanding how superconductivity emerges from correlated electronic states is a central challenge in condensed matter physics. The quasi-one-dimensional spin-ladder compound \bfs\ serves as a unique platform to study this interplay, as it lacks the two-dimensional square lattice characteristic of most iron-based superconductors. Here, we combine high-pressure x-ray and neutron diffraction, x-ray emission spectroscopy, and electrical transport to map its structural, magnetic, and electronic evolution into the superconducting regime. We \revised{observe} a striking pressure-induced decoupling: while the long-range stripe-type antiferromagnetic order remains remarkably robust under pressure up to the onset of superconductivity, the local iron magnetic moment is suppressed by nearly 80\%. This dichotomy \revised{points to an orbital-selective mechanism}, where specific Fe $3d$ electrons remain localized to sustain magnetism while others delocalize to form the itinerant and superconducting state. \revised{Superconductivity emerges while long-range magnetic order is still present, revealing that the two coexist in \bfs, which we attribute to} the selective response of multiorbital electronic degrees of freedom.
summary: This work investigates the interplay between superconductivity and magnetism in BaFe2S3 under high pressure using multiple techniques. Key findings show that the long-range magnetic order remains robust even as the local magnetic moment collapses. This suggests that superconductivity arises from an orbital-selective delocalization mechanism, where only specific electronic orbitals contribute to the itinerant superconducting state.
main_problem: The central challenge is understanding how superconductivity emerges from correlated electronic states, specifically investigating the interplay between superconductivity and magnetic order in a system lacking a 2D square lattice.
main_result: The study reveals a striking decoupling where long-range magnetic order persists while the local magnetic moment is suppressed, suggesting an orbital-selective mechanism.
method: The research combines high-pressure x-ray and neutron diffraction, X-ray emission spectroscopy (XES), and electrical transport measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is the quasi-one-dimensional spin-ladder compound BaFe2S3, which is studied across structural, magnetic, and electronic transitions under high pressure.
key_observables: Long-range ordered moment (neutron diffraction), local magnetic moment (XES), structural symmetry, and superconducting critical temperature (transport).
important_parameters: Pressure (up to 12-16.5 GPa), temperature (low T for transport), and the magnetic moment values ($\mu_B$).
main_assumptions: The interpretation relies on the 'orbital-selective mechanism' to explain the decoupling observed between the local moment and the long-range order.
figures_summary: Figures track structural transitions, the persistence of the stripe-type AFM structure up to high pressure, the continuous suppression of the local magnetic moment via XES, and the emergence of superconductivity in the normal state.
paper_structure: The paper systematically combines structural characterization (X-ray/Neutron) to map the phase diagram, magnetic measurements (Neutron/XES) to quantify magnetic order, and transport measurements (Resistivity) to locate the superconducting dome, culminating in the orbital-selective interpretation.
why_interesting: The concept of orbital-selective physics, where different electronic degrees of freedom respond differently to external tuning (like pressure), is highly relevant to understanding emergent quantum phases in strongly correlated materials.

figures.caption: Figure 1. Structural transition under pressure. Reconstruction of the reciprocal plane (H0L) at 15 K under (a) 0.3 GPa and (b) 1.5 GPa. At 0.3 GPa, Bragg reflections breaking the extinction conditions of the C centering (h+k ̸= 2n) expected in the Cmcm space group are present at odd H values (for K = 0), and are absent at 1.5 GPa.

Figure 2. Neutron diffraction under pressure. Powder neutron diffraction patterns of BaFe2S3 collected at 10 K (20 K for 2 and 5.5 GPa) under applied pressures ranging from 2 to 9.9 GPa. Only low-angle reflections are shown, labelled with their Miller indices (hkl). Patterns collected at 2 and 5.5 GPa were measured on the D1B diffractometer (λ = 2.52 Å), whereas those at 7.7 and 9.9 GPa were measured on D20 (λ = 2.42 Å). All patterns are rescaled to a common wavelength of 2.52 Å to facilitate comparison. Background has been subtracted and patterns are vertically offset for clarity.

Figure 3. Decoupling of local and ordered magnetic moments. (a) X-ray emission spectra (XES) of the Fe Kβ line at 300 K for BaFe2S3 and FeS2 (S = 0 reference) at various pressures. The inset shows a magnification of the Kβ ′ satellite region at ∼7055 eV. (b) Pressure dependence of the Fe ordered magnetic moment from powder neutron diffraction (PND) below 20 K (black squares, left axis); error bars represent refinement uncertainty. Red circles (right axis) show the local spin S at 300 K, extracted via integrated absolute difference (IAD) analysis and normalized to the ambient-pressure value S0.
